feature: Markdown nested HTML, list and quote paragraph boundaries
rootCauses: Closed HTML and nested containers incorrectly accepted unmarked paragraph continuation; trailing content could disappear.
Reparsed lists lost dequoted source columns and leaked lexer top-level state, changing tight-list paragraphs.
Quote marker transitions reinterpreted an existing paragraph as standalone HTML/code or split Setext heading content; manufactured terminators were mistaken for source blank lines.
fixes: Track the deepest open paragraph across nested lists and quotes, distinguish interrupting HTML from complete inline tags, and close containers at actual blank boundaries.
Preserve source lines and physical columns during reparsing; restore lexer and tokenizer methods even after failure.
Join supported Setext paragraph continuations without consuming following blocks; bound nested tracking and preserve recovery.

sourceRules.generation: Deterministic Cartesian combinations; no randomness. 14 body kinds x 5 endings x 7 containers plus 24 historical cases; 510 unique deeper combinations; 32 marker transitions.
sourceRules.deduplication: Initial nested exploration had 540 rows including 30 repeated sources; final corpus keeps 510 unique rows and original exploratory reports remain local.

oracles.policy: 18 retained reference-parser disagreements are separately reported; current reader follows primary CommonMark for these cases.

results.interaction: Restored tail anchor dispatch reaches target through actual onDomTap bridge; failed and late reads cannot replace CURRENT document.
results.recovery: 1000 quote marker transitions retain every VALUE; depth 257 reports explicit error and subsequent parses recover.

limits: Structural signatures normalize ordinary whitespace but preserve code text; Chrome checks visible body, exact pre text, marker visibility and container ancestry.
The screenshot comparison retains reader styling versus native reference styling; it is not pixel equivalence.
No WeChat WXML, DevTools or physical-device validation in this batch.
Not a complete CommonMark conformance claim; prior task-list/footnote dialect and full-spec differences outside this batch remain.
